questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The cultural and language oppotunitites of my destination were a major factor when I chose Vienna.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not very easy and the overall initial assistance regarding course registration, etc., was very poor. I had a single conversation with my receiving coordinator which did help out a lot, however, many important details regarding deadlines and especially my e-mail account linked to the university, were not explained to me before it was too late. This resulted in me not being able to take a full worth of ECTS points for the semester, which in hindsight was actually not too bad of a situation. The Erasmus team of students linked to the host university were very helpful and a big Erasmus Whatsapp group really helped a lot when one had a small, quick question.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance was not very elaborate. It would have been nice with a quick overview of course registration mechanics, your university e-mail adress and other minor stuff such as grading scales, etc. Primarily, the help I received was when I asked my fellow native students for assistance, which usually is also the best way to be introduced to a new system. My receiving coordinator was very helpful, although not very elaborate, and one could tell that she had a lot of other stuff going on, which one must respect of course, this, however, sometimes left me hanging for days waiting for e-mail replies and not fulfilling deadlines due to lack of awareness.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: All in all it was fine but it took a lot of effort and time to get just minor information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found my housing 6 months in advance so I did not have big issues. I would recommend this for anyone going to Vienna. I used the website
www.wg-gesucht.de
.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You usually won't have a sink next to the toilet, so after going you sometimes need to walk across a living room to acces the real bathroom where you'll find an operating sink and soap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Personally I did not have major problems with housing but I know for a fact the student housing in Vienna is scarce and a bunch of my fellow students had some minor issues with accomodations. This is, however, to be expected when trying to find a place to stay in a capital city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very challenging and I received no introduction at all.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: One has to puzzle together each and every course, juggling with courses worth only 2 ECTS points sometimes, and try to put together a program for the semester. Many course will overlap and one needs to either chose to find another course or just accept that you will miss a bunch of lectures. After finding the courses you wanna pick, you have to allocate points as a priority measure; each student has 1000 points and the more points you allocate to a course, the higher you prioritize it. Very confusing. Then, you have three different kind of courses, seminars, lectures, and übung, all of which will most of the time follow their own registration systems - some without points, some with points. I received almost no strategic advice on how to approach this system, so I had a very hard time figuring out what would be smartest to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None - except for a quick meeting with your receiving coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed, only after missing a few deadlines, to put together a program of 21 ECTS points, which my home university did not appreciate.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to be aware that course registration is an extremely time consuming process and you should start in good time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some excellent courses with very competent professors, covering my favorite subjects, so I coulnd't be happier.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was perfect, however, sometimes the workload did not match the ECTS points granted. 2 points for 15 lectures and 10 points for 45 lectures did not seem very rational to me in the long run, comparing to my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just brilliant - museums, concert houses, operas, coffe houses, shopping... Vienna has it all.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Orchestras and voice club were available but they were not too keen on taking in Erasmus students who were only there for 1 semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Concerts, operas and museums - it's just really good in Vienna.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing or hiking in the hills outside the city. Travel to Budapest for weekend or visit the balkan coastline.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As a Dane it was rather easy - the food is equally as disgusting as in Denmark so I had no struggle with that and the amount of beer being drunk is somewhat also similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope - I did not succeed very well in that due to Covid19 lockdown... Just talk with people, anyone you meet at your course, what other advice do you need?

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No sink by the toilet... rather disgusting sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that shopkeepers actually say 'hello' and 'goodbye' when you enter and leave a store makes you feel appreciated and welcome when shopping. It's a small thing but I already miss it. Also the coffee houses are brilliant - bring a book and just sit there for 3 hours drinking coffee and eating cake.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be VERY thourough with your course registration and start in good time
2. Go to language school, even just for a few weeks, it is really, really worth it and you will make good friends there
3. Participate in the initial Erasmus events - pretty basic advice but it is also really worth it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to buy a 'Semester Ticket' for the public transport. It is only €78 and you can ride the tram, bus and U-bahn anywhere in the city for the whole semester. Also, consider buying a 'Vorteilskart' with the ÖBB - it is very cheap, valid for a year and will save you up to 50% on train tickets if you feel like going skiing for visiting Salzburg for example.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really can't say - so many things happened during my 6 months stay, I can't possibly pick one single experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The course registration and generally just being thrown into a completely new university system with barely any introduction.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
